investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 124–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. Of the 6 total nodes in the cluster, 4 are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, leaving only 2 eligible nodes, both of which report insufficient capacity. Preemption was also unavailable on those 2 nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never received a vmId or remoteState value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259 to be fully unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for a new remote-agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The pod's node affinity or selector rules are too restrictive, confining scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes. If those rules were relaxed or additional nodes were labeled, capacity might be available.
Tertiary: A prior eval run or concurrent workload may have left orphaned remote-agent VMs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, exhausting the resource pool.

Lower confidence: A misconfiguration in the node resource advertisement (e.g., the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit set too low on the eligible nodes) could cause apparent exhaustion even when physical capacity exists.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. As a result, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, preemption was not possible (no victims found, and affinity-mismatched nodes cannot be helped by preemption). The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent as its first substantive step; because that call never produced a running pod, no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:264 was entirely unmet.
